proposal: This combo is not an untap loop but a bounce-and-recast loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds taps for X mana (X = greatest power among creatures you control, here 7+), then Temur Sabertooth's {1}{G} ability returns Selvala to hand (no untap ability is involved), Selvala is recast for its commander cost {1}{G}{G}, and Lightning Greaves (equip {0}) re-attaches to grant haste so the summoning-sick Selvala can tap again immediately. A fitting archetype would be a 'TapForManaBounceRecastLoop' parameterized by engine, bouncer, bounce_cost ({1}{G}), recast_cost ({1}{G}{G} plus commander tax growth), haste_enabler (Lightning Greaves) with attach_cost ({0}), activation_cost ({G}), yield_expr GREATEST_POWER_AMONG_OWN_CREATURES, and a profit invariant of yield minus per-cycle costs (~5 mana) > 0; the loop also generates infinite ETB/LTB and storm triggers per cycle, which the untap archetype cannot model.

This combo is a bounce-and-recast mana loop, not an untap loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds taps for X = greatest power among your creatures (needs a power-6+ creature), Temur Sabertooth's '{1}{G}: return another creature you control to hand' bounces Selvala instead of untapping her, and she is recast for {1}{G}{G} and can re-tap immediately only because Concordant Crossroads grants haste. A new archetype (e.g. BounceRecastManaLoop) would need params: engine (Selvala, activation_cost {G}, pool_color G, yield GREATEST_POWER_AMONG_OWN_CREATURES), bouncer (Temur Sabertooth, bounce_cost {1}{G}, nontargeted, bounces to owner's hand), engine_recast_cost {1}{G}{G} paid each cycle (plus commander-tax awareness since Selvala is the commander), a required haste_enabler on the battlefield (Concordant Crossroads), and profit_invariant yield - 5 > 0; the loop additionally produces infinite ETB/LTB triggers, storm count, and (via Selvala's own trigger) card draw as side products, which TapForManaUntapLoop cannot model since it assumes the engine stays on the battlefield and merely untaps.

This combo is a bounce-and-recast loop, not a tap-untap loop: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds ({G}, {T}) adds X mana equal to the greatest power among creatures you control, Temur Sabertooth ({1}{G}) returns Selvala to hand instead of untapping her, Selvala is recast for her mana cost {1}{G}{G}, and Surrak and Goreclaw grants the re-entering Selvala haste (plus a +1/+1 counter) so she can tap again immediately. A fitting new archetype would be 'TapForManaBounceRecastLoop' with params: engine (the mana creature), bouncer, bounce_cost, engine_recast_cost, haste_granter (static permanent removing summoning sickness on re-entry), activation_cost, per_cycle_counter_pump (power gained per re-entry from ETB counters, non-cumulative since counters are lost on bounce), pool_color, and a profit invariant of yield minus (activation + bounce + recast) > 0; each cycle also generates one ETB/LTB/cast trigger for storm and blink payoffs.

This combo is a three-piece chained untap loop that does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop's two-piece (engine + untapper) shape: Gaea's Cradle is the mana engine ({T}: Add {G} for each creature you control, at least {G}{G}{G}{G}{G} given five creatures), Voyaging Satyr is the primary untapper ({T}: Untap target land, targeting the Cradle), but the Satyr cannot re-ready itself — it requires a second untapper, Staff of Domination ({3}, {T}: Untap target creature, targeting the Satyr; then {1}: Untap Staff of Domination to reset itself). Binding Satyr as 'untapper' with untapper_reset_cost {4} would misrepresent the reset as a self-ability and omit Staff of Domination from the binding entirely, so simulation would not exercise the actual pieces. A new archetype such as ChainedTapForManaUntapLoop is needed, with params: engine (Gaea's Cradle, activation_cost {0}, dynamic yield GG*CREATURES_YOU_CONTROL, pool_color G), untapper_1 (Voyaging Satyr, untap_cost {0}, targets engine), untapper_2 (Staff of Domination, untap_cost {3}, targets untapper_1, self_reset_cost {1}), net profit per cycle = creatures_you_control - 4 > 0 (hence the five-creature prerequisite), with Staff's {5} draw ability as the DRAW_LOOP stage payoff.

This combo is not an untap loop — Sanctum Weaver never untaps; instead Temur Sabertooth's {1}{G} activation bounces the Weaver to hand, it is recast for {1}{G}, and Concordant Crossroads grants haste so it can tap again the same turn. A new archetype, e.g. BounceRecastManaLoop, is needed with params: engine (Sanctum Weaver, a creature tapped for X mana where X scales with enchantments controlled), bouncer (Temur Sabertooth), bounce_cost ({1}{G}), recast_cost (the engine's mana cost {1}{G}), haste_enabler (Concordant Crossroads, required because the engine re-enters each cycle), yield_expr (COUNT_OWN_ENCHANTMENTS, noting the Weaver itself is an enchantment creature so the count dips by one while it is off the battlefield), pool_color (any one color, engine's choice), and a profit_invariant of yield - 4 > 0 per cycle (X mana in vs {1}{G} bounce + {1}{G} recast), matching the 'at least four enchantments' prerequisite; the loop additionally produces infinite ETB/LTB triggers and storm count as side effects.

Copy-spell ETB loop: cast a token-copying sorcery (Twinflame) targeting any creature you control, then flash in Dualcaster Mage holding priority; its ETB trigger copies Twinflame targeting Dualcaster Mage itself, and each resolved copy creates a hasty token copy of Dualcaster Mage whose own ETB copies Twinflame again, yielding arbitrarily many hasty attackers plus infinite ETB/LTB and magecraft triggers. Suggested archetype 'CopySpellTokenLoop' with params: copy_spell (Twinflame, cost {1}{R}), etb_copier (Dualcaster Mage, cost {1}{R}{R}, flash), copier_targets_spell true, token_haste true, tokens_exiled_at_end_step true, total_entry_cost {2}{R}{R}{R}; win condition is combat with N hasty tokens before the end-step exile, entry_phase MAIN1 (pre-combat).

This combo is a spell-copy mana loop, not a tap/untap permanent loop: Jeska's Will (a sorcery) is cast once to add {R} per card in a target opponent's hand (7+), and Reiterate with buyback ({4}{R}{R} total) copies it on the stack, returning to hand each resolution so it can copy the Will again each cycle, netting mana per iteration and generating infinite red mana, storm, and magecraft triggers. A fitting archetype would be something like BuybackCopyManaLoop with params: source_spell (the mana-producing instant/sorcery on the stack), copier (the buyback copy spell), copier_total_cost (e.g. "{4}{R}{R}"), yield_expr (e.g. TARGET_OPPONENT_HAND_SIZE for {R} produced per copy), profit_invariant (yield - 6 > 0), initial_cast_cost of the source spell ({2}{R}), plus a requirement that the source spell remain on the stack (hold priority) for the first copy.

This combo is a spell-copy buyback loop, not a permanent-untap loop: Mana Geyser (a sorcery) is cast once, then Reiterate with buyback ({4}{R}{R} total, {1}{R}{R} plus buyback {3}) repeatedly copies the Geyser on the stack while returning Reiterate to hand, with each copy adding {R} per tapped land opponents control (at least seven). A fitting archetype would be something like SpellCopyBuybackManaLoop with params: mana_spell (the copied instant/sorcery), copier (the buyback spell), mana_spell_cost, copier_total_cost (base plus buyback), yield_expr (e.g. COUNT_TAPPED_OPPONENT_LANDS), pool_color, and a profit invariant like yield - 6 > 0, plus tracking of magecraft/storm triggers as byproducts; entry would be MAIN1 with the prerequisite that opponents control at least seven tapped lands.

This combo is a one-shot token-copy damage burst, not a tap/untap mana loop: Devastating Onslaught (cast for {10}{R}, X=5) creates five token copies of Terror of the Peaks with haste, and each token entering triggers every other Terror of the Peaks' enter-the-battlefield damage ability, dealing power-based damage (5 each) across up to 25 triggers for ~125 total damage before the tokens are sacrificed at the next end step. A suitable executor archetype would be something like 'TokenCopyEtbBurstDamage' with params: copy_spell (Devastating Onslaught), copy_target/engine (Terror of the Peaks), copies_created (X), damage_per_trigger (engine power), trigger_count formula (X*(X+1) minus self-triggers), total_cost ({10}{R}), and damage targeting policy (divide among opponents/creatures).

This combo does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop: no permanent is tapped for mana and nothing untaps. It is a cast-bounce mana loop: an engine creature (Grinning Ignus) is cast from hand for {2}{R}, triggering a counter-accumulator (Runaway Steam-Kin) that adds a +1/+1 counter per red spell cast; the engine's activated ability ({R}, return self to hand) adds {C}{C}{R}, and every third counter-batch on the accumulator is cashed in (remove three counters: add {R}{R}{R}) to keep the loop mana-neutral. A fitting archetype would be 'CastBounceStormLoop' with params: engine (creature cast from hand), cast_cost ({2}{R}), bounce_cost ({R}), bounce_yield ({C}{C}{R}), accumulator (Runaway Steam-Kin), accumulator_trigger_condition (cast a red spell, fewer than 3 counters), accumulator_cashout (remove 3 counters: add {R}{R}{R}), sorcery_speed_restriction (true), producing infinite ETB/LTB and storm count rather than net mana; payoffs would be ETB/storm win conditions not listed in this combo's steps.

This combo is a spell-copy ETB loop, not a tap-untap mana loop: Dualcaster Mage's enters-the-battlefield trigger copies the still-on-stack Devastating Onslaught targeting Dualcaster Mage itself, the copy creates a token copy of Dualcaster Mage, whose ETB trigger copies Onslaught again, repeating for infinite hasty Dualcaster Mage tokens, infinite ETB triggers, and infinite magecraft triggers. A suitable archetype would be something like SpellCopyEtbTokenLoop with params: copy_spell (the instant/sorcery whose copy creates the token, e.g. Devastating Onslaught), etb_copier (the creature whose ETB copies a spell, e.g. Dualcaster Mage), copy_spell_cost ({2}{R}), copier_cost ({1}{R}{R}), copier_needs_flash_hold_priority (true), loop_yield (hasty token copies of etb_copier per iteration), and a note that tokens are sacrificed at the next end step so the win must convert via combat or triggers the same turn.

This combo is a three-piece chained untap loop that TapForManaUntapLoop cannot express: the engine (Gaea's Cradle, '{T}: Add {G} for each creature you control', yield scales with creature count and requires at least five creatures for profit) is untapped by a creature untapper (Voyaging Satyr, '{T}: Untap target land'), but the Satyr cannot re-ready itself — a second untapper (Staff of Domination) must pay {3},{T} to untap the Satyr and then {1} to untap itself, for a net cost of {4} per cycle against a yield of CREATURES_YOU_CONTROL green mana. A new archetype, e.g. ChainedTapForManaUntapLoop, would need params for engine, primary_untapper (targets engine, type land), secondary_untapper (targets primary_untapper, cost {3}, self-reset cost {1}), activation_cost {0} (Cradle taps free), pool_color G, yield_expr CREATURES_YOU_CONTROL, and profit_invariant yield - 4 > 0; payoffs would be Staff of Domination's own {5} draw ability after infinite mana.

This combo is a spell-copy buyback loop, not a tap/untap permanent loop: Jeska's Will (a sorcery) is cast once, then Reiterate with buyback {3} (total {4}{R}{R}) repeatedly copies it on the stack, with each copy adding {R} equal to a targeted opponent's hand size (>=7). A fitting archetype would be 'BuybackCopyRitualLoop' with params: ritual_spell (the copied mana-producing spell, e.g. Jeska's Will), ritual_cast_cost ({2}{R}), copier (Reiterate), copier_cost_with_buyback ({4}{R}{R}), yield_expr (CARDS_IN_TARGET_OPPONENT_HAND, min 7 {R} per cycle), profit_invariant (yield - 6 > 0), target_requirement (opponent with >=7 cards in hand), pool_color (R), plus produced loop outputs (infinite red mana, storm count, magecraft triggers); entry_phase MAIN1 with the initial spell resolving only after enough copies are stacked or after each copy resolves before recasting via buyback-returned Reiterate.

Instant/sorcery buyback-copy mana loop: cast a mana-producing spell (Mana Geyser, {3}{R}{R}, adds {R} per tapped land opponents control), then repeatedly cast Reiterate with buyback ({4}{R}{R}) targeting the copyable mana spell on the stack; each resolved copy nets mana (>=7 red minus the {4}{R}{R} buyback cost) while Reiterate returns to hand, yielding infinite red mana, storm count, and magecraft triggers. A fitting archetype would parameterize: mana_spell, mana_spell_cost, copy_spell, copy_spell_buyback_cost, yield_expr (e.g. COUNT_TAPPED_OPPONENT_LANDS), profit_invariant (yield - 6 > 0), and pool_color R; entry phase any with priority, typically opponents' end step or MAIN1 after opponents tap lands.

This combo is not a tap-for-mana untap loop; it is a one-shot token-copy damage burst. A fitting archetype would be 'TokenCopyEnterDamageBurst': cast a copy-spell (Devastating Onslaught, cost {X...}{R} with X=5 here, total {10}{R}) targeting a creature with an enters-trigger damage ability (Terror of the Peaks). Params would include copy_spell, copy_count (X), trigger_source (Terror of the Peaks), damage_per_trigger_expr (entering creature's power, 5), and total_damage_expr (with N tokens entering one at a time, the original triggers N times and each token triggers for tokens entering after it, yielding damage = power * (N + N*(N-1)/2 + ...); per the steps, 5 tokens produce 25 triggers of 5 damage = 125 damage divided among any targets). Entry phase MAIN1; payoffs are none beyond the direct damage.

This combo is a cast-bounce loop, not a tap/untap mana loop: Grinning Ignus is cast for {2}{R}, triggering Runaway Steam-Kin to add a +1/+1 counter, then Ignus's ability ({R}, return it to hand) adds {C}{C}{R}, netting mana back toward recasting; every three casts Steam-Kin's counters convert to {R}{R}{R}, making the loop self-sustaining. A fitting archetype would be a 'CastBounceStormLoop' with params: bounce_engine (creature cast repeatedly, e.g. Grinning Ignus), cast_cost ({2}{R}), bounce_activation_cost ({R}), bounce_mana_yield ({C}{C}{R}), ramp_engine (Runaway Steam-Kin), ramp_trigger_condition (cast a red spell, <3 counters), ramp_payout_cost (remove three +1/+1 counters), ramp_payout ({R}{R}{R}), timing_restriction (sorcery-speed only), producing infinite ETB/LTB and storm count as payoff hooks rather than infinite pooled mana.

This combo is a cast-bounce loop, not a tap/untap loop: Mox Amber taps for one colored mana (given a matching legendary creature), a second cheap permanent is cast with that mana, Hullbreaker Horror's cast trigger returns Mox Amber to hand, Mox Amber is recast for {0}, and its second Horror trigger returns the other permanent to hand — netting infinite casts, ETB/LTB triggers, storm count, and colored mana if the recast cycle nets positive. A suitable new archetype would be a ZeroCostRecastBounceLoop with params: bounce_engine (Hullbreaker Horror, a cast-trigger bouncer on the battlefield), free_permanent (Mox Amber, castable for {0}), secondary_permanent (any castable-at-profit permanent such as Sol Ring named in the steps), mana_source (Mox Amber's tap ability with its legendary-creature color condition as a precondition), per-cycle mana delta, and produced resources [storm, ETB, LTB, colored mana].

This combo does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop: the untap ability is intrinsic to the engine (Basalt Monolith's own '{3}: Untap this artifact'), and Rings of Brighthearth neither grants nor activates an untap ability — it is a static trigger that COPIES the engine's non-mana activated ability for an additional {2}. Propose a new archetype 'SelfUntapAbilityCopyLoop' with params: engine (Basalt Monolith, taps for {C}{C}{C} at activation_cost {0}), self_untap_cost ({3}, the engine's own untap activation), copier (Rings of Brighthearth), copy_cost ({2}, paid when the copy trigger resolves), engine_mana_value (3), copier_mana_value (3), pool_color (C). Loop per cycle: tap engine for 3, activate self-untap for 3, pay 2 to copy it via the copier, resolve copy to untap, tap for 3 again, resolve original untap — producing 6 and spending 5 for net +{C} per cycle (profit_invariant: 6 - 5 > 0), requiring {2} starting mana to prime the first copy; produces infinite colorless mana with no payoff cards listed in the combo steps.

This combo is a cast-bounce mana loop, not a tap-untap loop: Sol Ring is never untapped in place, it is returned to hand by Tidespout Tyrant's cast trigger and recast. A new archetype (e.g. CastBounceManaLoop) would need params for the bouncer (Tidespout Tyrant, a battlefield permanent whose 'whenever you cast a spell' trigger returns a target permanent to hand), the engine artifact (Sol Ring, cast_cost {1}, tap ability adding {C}{C}), and a secondary castable-with-{C} nontoken permanent used to alternate bounce targets so Sol Ring can tap between recasts; each cycle nets +1 colorless mana ({C}{C} produced minus {1} to recast Sol Ring, with the filler permanent's cost covered by loop surplus once established) and +2 storm count, yielding infinite colorless mana and infinite storm.

This combo is a recastable-draw loop, not a mana/untap loop: Sensei's Divining Top taps to draw a card and put itself on top of its owner's library, The Reality Chip (attached to a creature) permits casting spells from the top of the library, and Etherium Sculptor reduces the Top's {1} cost to {0}, so each cycle nets a free draw, a draw trigger, and a storm/cast count with no mana spent. A fitting archetype would be 'SelfTopdeckRecastLoop' with params: engine (the permanent that returns itself to the library, e.g. Sensei's Divining Top), engine_activation_cost (tap, no mana), topdeck_cast_enabler (The Reality Chip, required attached state), cost_reducer (Etherium Sculptor), effective_recast_cost ({0} after reduction), per_cycle_yield (1 card drawn + 1 cast trigger), and entry requirement that the enabler is attached to a creature; payoffs would be any draw-trigger or storm win conditions.

This combo is a recast-draw loop, not a tap-for-mana-untap loop: Sensei's Divining Top's {T} ability draws a card and puts Top on the library, The Reality Chip (attached to a creature) allows casting it from the top of the library, and Foundry Inspector reduces its {1} cost to {0}, so each cycle nets a free draw and a storm/cast trigger with no mana or untapper involved. A fitting archetype would be something like SelfRecastDrawLoop with params: engine (Sensei's Divining Top), cast_enabler (The Reality Chip, with attachment-state requirement), cost_reducer (Foundry Inspector), effective_recast_cost ({0}), draw_per_cycle (1), storm_per_cycle (1), plus payoff hooks for draw-trigger or cast-trigger win conditions.

This combo is a recursion/storm loop, not a tap-untap mana loop: Sensei's Divining Top (cost reduced to {0} by Etherium Sculptor) is repeatedly cast, each cast triggers Forensic Gadgeteer to investigate for a Clue token; the Clue is tapped to Urza, Lord High Artificer's ability for {U}, Top's {T} ability draws a card and puts itself on top of the library, then the Clue is sacrificed for {1} (Gadgeteer's reduction) to draw Top back into hand and recast it. A fitting executor archetype would be something like 'RecastTriggerLoop' with params: recastable_piece (Sensei's Divining Top), effective_cast_cost ({0}), cast_trigger_source (Forensic Gadgeteer), token_produced (Clue), token_use (tap to Urza for {U} then sacrifice for {1} to draw), self_return_ability (Top's {T} draw-and-top ability), producing net-zero mana per cycle with infinite draw triggers and storm count.

This combo is a bounce-and-recast loop, not a tap/untap loop: Mana Vault ({1}, taps for {C}{C}{C}) is cast, tapped for mana, then returned to its owner's hand by Tidespout Tyrant's cast trigger (which fires off another {C}{C}-castable nontoken permanent's recast), and recast at a profit of {2} per cycle. A fitting archetype would be a BounceRecastManaLoop with params: bouncer (permanent with a 'whenever you cast a spell, return target permanent to hand' trigger, e.g. Tidespout Tyrant), engine (cheap mana rock cast+tapped each cycle, e.g. Mana Vault), engine_cast_cost ('{1}'), engine_tap_yield ('{C}{C}{C}'), shuttle (a second nontoken permanent castable for {C}{C} that alternates being bounced/recast with the engine), shuttle_cast_cost ('{C}{C}'), net_mana_per_cycle ('{C}{C}' minus shuttle recast if alternating), pool_color ('C'), plus outputs infinite colorless mana and infinite storm count; entry_phase MAIN1.

This combo is a recast-draw loop, not a mana loop: Sensei's Divining Top's {T} ability draws a card and puts itself on top of its owner's library; The Reality Chip (attached to a creature) permits casting spells from the top of the library; and Cloud Key (artifact chosen) reduces Top's {1} cast cost to {0}, so each cycle is tap-Top-to-draw, then recast Top from the library for free, yielding infinite card draw, draw triggers, and storm count with no mana engine or untapper. A suitable archetype would be something like SelfRestackRecastLoop with params: engine (the self-restacking permanent, e.g. Sensei's Divining Top), library_cast_enabler (e.g. The Reality Chip with its attachment condition), cost_reducer (e.g. Cloud Key with chosen type), net_recast_cost (effective cost per cycle, here {0}), per_cycle_yield ("1 card drawn, 1 draw trigger, 1 storm count"), and a guard that the loop only nets cards while net_recast_cost is {0} (otherwise it consumes mana per card).

This combo is a cast-trigger bounce loop, not a tap/untap loop: with Tidespout Tyrant on the battlefield, casting Mox Amber (mana value 0) triggers Tyrant to return a permanent to its owner's hand; tapping Mox Amber for mana (requires a colored legendary creature or planeswalker) and casting the bounced permanent triggers Tyrant again to bounce Mox Amber itself, allowing it to be recast for {0} and retapped each iteration, producing infinite storm count and infinite colored mana. A new archetype such as BounceRecastManaLoop would need params: bouncer (Tidespout Tyrant, on battlefield, cast-trigger returning target permanent to hand), recastable_engine (Mox Amber), engine_cast_cost ({0}), engine_tap_yield (one mana of any color among legendary creatures/planeswalkers controlled), secondary_recast_piece (any nontoken permanent castable off one Mox Amber activation), legendary_prerequisite (true), and per-cycle outputs (storm +2, net mana >= 0), with entry_phase MAIN1.

This combo does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop: there is no untap effect. It is a cast-bounce loop — a new archetype like CastBounceStormLoop would need: bouncer (Tidespout Tyrant, a battlefield permanent whose cast-trigger returns a target permanent to its owner's hand), free_engine (Mox Opal, a zero-cost artifact that taps for one mana of any color, gated by metalcraft: control three or more artifacts), and a secondary cheap spell castable with one colored mana. Each cycle: cast Mox Opal for {0}, Tyrant trigger bounces the cheap permanent to hand, tap Opal for one mana, recast the cheap permanent, Tyrant trigger bounces Opal back to hand; the mana is net-neutral and each iteration adds two casts to the storm count, yielding infinite storm (and infinite cast/ETB/bounce triggers) rather than infinite mana. Prerequisites the executor must verify: metalcraft holds throughout (three or more artifacts besides the cycling Opal, or counting it appropriately) and the returned permanent is nontoken.

This combo is a cast-recast draw loop, not a tap/untap mana loop: Sensei's Divining Top is cast for {0} (Foundry Inspector's reduction), Forensic Gadgeteer investigates on the cast to make a Clue, Urza taps the Clue artifact for {U}, the Top taps to draw a card and put itself on top of the library, and the Clue is sacrificed for {1} (Gadgeteer's activation discount) to draw the Top back into hand, repeating for infinite draw and storm. A fitting archetype would be 'CastTriggerRecycleLoop' with params: recycled_spell (the zero-cost spell recast each cycle, here Sensei's Divining Top), cast_cost_after_reductions ({0}), cast_trigger_source (Forensic Gadgeteer, producing a Clue per cast), resource_token (Clue), token_sink_cost ({1} after discount), mana_source (Urza, Lord High Artificer tapping an artifact for {U}), self_return_mechanism (Top's {T} draw ability putting itself on library), net_mana_per_cycle (0 or positive), and per-cycle yields (cards drawn, storm count, draw triggers).

This combo is a cast-bounce-recast loop, not an untap loop: Tidespout Tyrant's cast trigger returns Grim Monolith (or another {C}-castable nontoken permanent) to hand, and Grim Monolith is recast for {2} then tapped for {C}{C}{C}, netting {C} and one storm count per cycle. A fitting archetype would be a BounceRecastManaLoop with params: bouncer (Tidespout Tyrant, on battlefield), engine (Grim Monolith, cast from hand), engine_cast_cost ({2}), engine_tap_yield ({C}{C}{C}), a secondary bounce target (any nontoken permanent castable with {C}) to alternate triggers, net_mana_per_cycle (+{C}), plus infinite storm count as a secondary product; entry_phase MAIN1.

This combo is not a tap/untap mana loop — no permanent is ever untapped. It is a recast-cycle loop: Sensei's Divining Top is cast for {0} (Cloud Key reduces {1} to {0}), Forensic Gadgeteer triggers on the artifact cast to investigate, Urza taps the fresh Clue token for {U}, Top's {T} ability draws a card and puts Top back on the library, and the Clue is sacrificed for {1} (Gadgeteer's activation discount) to draw Top back into hand, restarting the cycle. A fitting archetype would be a 'CastTriggerRecycleLoop' parameterized by: recurring_spell (Sensei's Divining Top), spell_cast_cost ('{0}' after reductions), cast_trigger_source (Forensic Gadgeteer) producing a token resource (Clue), token_conversion_cost ('{1}' after reductions) yielding a draw, mana_source (Urza, Lord High Artificer tapping the token artifact for {U}), self_return_ability (Top's '{T}: Draw a card, put Top on top of library'), with net loop cost zero and outputs of infinite draw triggers, infinite card draw, and near-infinite storm count.

This combo does not fit TapForManaUntapLoop: there is no named mana-producing engine permanent (the prerequisites only require generic 'nonland mana sources that tap for at least {4}'), and the untap effect comes from a spell held on the stack being repeatedly copied, not from an activated untap ability. Proposed archetype: SpellCopyUntapLoop — params: copied_spell (an instant/sorcery that untaps all nonland permanents you control, e.g. Dramatic Reversal, cast once and held on the stack with priority retained), copier (a permanent with a tap ability that copies a target instant or sorcery you control, e.g. Lithoform Engine), copy_cost (the copier's activation mana cost, e.g. '{3}'), spell_mana_value, copier_mana_value, and mana_floor (minimum mana the battlefield's nonland sources must produce per untap, here '{4}'); profit invariant: per-cycle mana produced minus copy_cost > 0, since the copier itself is untapped by each copy's resolution.

A recurring-protection lock, not a mana loop: each turn Drafna, Founder of Lat-Nam pays {1}{U} to bounce The One Ring to hand, then The One Ring is recast for {4}; its enters trigger (only when cast) grants protection from everything until your next turn, and the bounce also resets burden counters so the upkeep life loss never accumulates. A fitting archetype would be a 'BounceRecastETBLoop' with params: bouncer (Drafna), recurred_permanent (The One Ring), bounce_cost ({1}{U}), recast_cost ({4}), etb_effect (protection from everything until next turn), cadence (once per turn), entry_phase MAIN1, payoffs [] (soft lock, no direct win conversion).

This is a three-piece copy-loop that doesn't fit TapForManaUntapLoop's two-piece engine/untapper schema: Tezzeret the Seeker activates [+1] (untap up to two target artifacts) once per turn, and Lithoform Engine ({2}, {T}) copies that loyalty activation each cycle, retargeting the copy at Mana Vault and Lithoform Engine itself. Each cycle taps Mana Vault for {C}{C}{C}, pays {2} to Lithoform Engine, and the resolved copy untaps both artifacts, netting {C} per iteration for infinite colorless mana and infinite artifact untaps.
